messages:
maria: Quick sync: we need to settle the edge-decider API shape before the next runtime cut. main goals: safe rollback, minimal RTT impact, and no accidental incompatible responses to old runtimes.
jonathan: +1. Is the primary concern the schema drift or behavioural mismatches (preemption/affinity)?
anita: both. Schema drift we can mitigate with versioned fields, behavioral mismatches are trickier — the runtime expects guarantees (e.g. stable affinity) today.
ravi: my 2c: include a capability handshake. runtime -> policy: 'capabilities': ["preemptible","region_hint","kv_cache_v2"] so policy can avoid handing back decisions that runtime can't satisfy.
maria: agreed. also want a decision_id and a stable_decision_hash for dedupe/replay protection.
jonathan: sketch of minimal response shape (proto-ish):
```
Decision {
  string decision_id;
  string version; // policy version that produced this decision
  repeated string route_candidates; // ordered by preference
  string chosen_route; // single best-fit
  map<string,string> hints; // e.g. {"region":"eu-west-1","model_variant":"gptq-8b"}
  bool preemptible = false; // runtime may evict if constrained
  int32 ttl_seconds; // how long this decision is valid for
  string stable_hash; // deterministic hash across policy evals for tracing
  repeated string compatibility_warnings; // human readable for ops
}
```
anita: two important semantics: 1) if preemptible=true, runtime must be allowed to evict after grace_window; 2) chosen_route must be one of route_candidates. no silent mapping.
ravi: for rollback safety: require the runtime to refuse decisions from unknown policy versions unless policy includes a backwards_compatible flag. Also emit telemetry when runtime rejects a decision.
maria: telemetry: increment counters: decision_accepted, decision_rejected(reason), decision_applied_latency, decision_fallback_triggered. make them taggable by tenant and model_family.
jonathan: latency concern: adding capability handshake adds RTT. proposal: handshake cached per runtime instance with a TTL and exchanged asynchronously at runtime bootstrap. policy should fallback to a conservative default if handshake absent.
anita: +1. conservative default = treat runtime as minimal-capable (no preemption, no region hints). policy must then avoid giving preemptible=true.
ravi: edge case: canary policy that relies on preemption for lower-cost model variants. For canary rollout we should gate via explicit "canary_token" in decision, runtime will only honor canary decisions if it was flagged during bootstrap. prevents accidental org-wide rollouts.
maria: good. also add an invariant check: runtime validates that chosen_route matches one candidate and that ttl <= max_ttl_by_tenant. If invalid -> reject with rejection reason; policy must surface a fallback decision.
jonathan: on compatibility_warnings: we should limit free-form text. prefer structured codes so we can alert: e.g. WARNING_CODE_MISSING_KV_CACHE, WARNING_CODE_REGION_MISMATCH.
anita: agreed. ops want quick alerting.
ravi: deployment flow: policy runtime changes first -> enable compatibility mode for N hours -> enable strict mode via feature flag -> monitor decision_rejected spikes -> flip. we should codify this in the rollout checklist.
maria: action items: jonathan to write a short RFC with proto + handshake spec; anita to add runtime validation tests; ravi to add metrics and alert rules draft. I'll add a short dashboard mock for decision rejects.
deploy-bot: Started CI job #4521 for branch "edge-decider-api-spec" — build 1/3.
jonathan: I'll aim to post the RFC by EOD tomorrow. any objections to adding stable_hash as decision-level (not per-candidate) trace ID?
anita: fine. helps on replay debugging. ensure we hash on canonicalized candidate list so order changes are deliberate.
maria: tiny nit: name the field stable_decision_fingerprint to avoid confusion with tracing IDs.
jonathan: ack. thanks all.
maria: closing — if no more comments, i'll merge the checklist to the architecture board and we can pick this up in eng-platform sync on Thursday. :thumbsup:
